baby-girl.why: ORTHOGRAPHY DEFECT: 'Baby Mädchen' is written with a SPACE. German does not space compound nouns — this is a Deppenleerzeichen and is simply wrong for a word projected on a board and read aloud to children. The minimum, same-word fix is the hyphen (Duden permits the Bindestrich in compounds with a foreign first element): Baby-Mädchen. SEPARATE, LARGER ISSUE FOR THE OPERATOR, deliberately NOT fixed here because it would be a different lemma: 'Baby-Mädchen' is not idiomatic German — a native would say 'Mädchen', or 'Kleinkind' for the pictured walking child. The art also shows a toddler, not a baby. Recommend a lemma review of this key.

blocks.why: plural-picture: the art shows FIVE blocks, so the displayed/spoken label must be the plural. The field holds the SINGULAR 'Bauklotz' — a child sees five blocks and hears 'Bauklotz'. classification.json's own reason for this key says the same: 'for a plural-picture the displayed label should be the plural form (Baukloetze / klossar / blocs)'. Duden gives the plural as Bauklötze (umgangssprachlich also Bauklötzer); Bauklötze is the standard form. Compare the coherent sisters: cards holds 'Karten' and boots holds 'Stiefel', both already plurals. NOTE: this reverses the previous de-02 round, which fixed this row the OPPOSITE way (to 'Bauklotz') — that round recorded no image_seen and so never saw that five blocks are pictured.

diplodocus.why: Duden's German headword is Diplodokus (germanised -k-), not the Latin genus spelling. Since the plural must come from Duden, the singular has to travel with it — leaving `Diplodocus` beside a k-plural would be an orthographic mongrel. Same word, spelling corrected. (Recording the counter-argument: `Diplodocus` as the Latin genus name is not itself illiterate; if the operator prefers it, the consistent plural would be Diplodocen. But DUDEN WINS is the rule, and Duden prints only Diplodokus/Diplodoken.)

french-fries.why: Capitalisation. Duden's headword is 'Pommes frites, die' — 'frites' is LOWERCASE (it is the French adjective, not a German noun). The stored 'Pommes Frites' is a misspelling. Also worth recording: Duden classes the word as a PLURALWORT ('nur im Plural'), so there is no singular at all — which matches the plural-picture classification: the label IS the plural. Pure form correction of the same word, hence FIX rather than PLURALIA_TANTUM.

jelly-beans.why: plural-picture, but the label field holds the SINGULAR 'Geleebohne' while the art shows a heap of ~13 beans. Per RULE 3 the label IS the plural for this category, and the sibling plural-picture rows prove the convention: ice-skates holds 'Schlittschuhe' (a pair → plural), lights holds 'Lichterkette' (one string of lights → singular, correctly). This row is the outlier. Pure form correction of the same lemma (Bohne → Bohnen), not a lemma change.

pickup-truck.why: Duden's headword is hyphenated: 'der Pick-up' — 'kleinerer Lieferwagen mit Pritsche', which is exactly a pickup truck. The stored unhyphenated 'Pickup' is common in running German but is not Duden's Rechtschreibung, and Duden is THE authority for German orthography. This is a pure orthographic correction of the SAME word, so FIX (not HOLD) is the right class. The prior de-08 file passed this OK/OK/OK without fetching. Flagging that this row has no art, so the lemma choice cannot be checked against a picture — only the spelling is being ruled on.

potato-chips.why: The plural-picture convention is broken here, and this batch contains its own controls. category=plural-picture means 'the label IS the plural' — and the two sibling plural-labels in this very batch obey it (peas → Erbsen/Erbsen; pretzels → Brezeln/Brezeln). potato-chips instead stores the SINGULAR 'Kartoffelchip', so the board would show a bag of crisps captioned with the word for ONE crisp. Duden backs the plural label independently: 'der Kartoffelchip; Plural: die Kartoffelchips (MEIST IM PLURAL)'. Same lemma, plural form → FIX, not HOLD. (The prior de-08 file 'fixed' this to 'Kartoffelchip' — the value it already held, a no-op.)

slippers.why: The singular field holds a SINGULAR (Hausschuh) on a plural-picture row. The art is a PAIR and the row is classified plural-picture/hasPlural:false, which per the brief means 'the label IS the plural' — so the singular field must carry the plural form, as every sibling plural-picture key in this batch already does: shoes='Schuhe', sneakers='Turnschuhe', snow-boots='Schneestiefel'. slippers is the one odd row out. Pure form correction of the SAME word (Hausschuh->Hausschuhe, Duden-attested), not a lemma change, so FIX. The brief also names sandals/slippers as genuine two-object PAIRS, which the picture confirms.

baby-girl.why: Same space-to-hyphen fix. The plural itself is correctly a zero plural: das Mädchen to die Mädchen (-chen diminutive), so only the spacing is at fault.

basketball.why: REAL DEFECT — the stored plural is a zero echo of the singular, and the dictionary gives an umlaut plural. Duden Grammatik verbatim: 'der Basketball; Genitiv: des Basketball[e]s, Plural: die Basketbälle'; en.wiktionary agrees: 'Basketball m (strong, genitive Basketballes or Basketballs, plural Basketbälle)'. Duden does also mark a separate sport reading 'ohne Plural; meist ohne Artikel' — but that reading does not apply here: the picture is unambiguously a ball, there is no ART_DEFECT flag on this row, and the classification (countable-thing / hasGender / hasPlural TRUE) independently says the same. A ball is countable and its plural is Basketbälle. This is exactly the umlaut class the brief says the builder cannot do (Hand to Hände) — and note beach-ball in this same batch DOES carry its umlaut plural (Wasserbälle), which is what makes this one visibly unauthored.

beetroot.why: The stored plural is a zero echo of the singular and is not an attested form. The head noun inflects: Duden Grammatik for Bete verbatim: 'die Bete; Genitiv: der Bete, Plural: die Beten'; en.wiktionary gives the phrase directly: 'Rote Bete f ... plural Rote Beten'. (Duden has no standalone 'Rote Bete' headword — only Bete and the compound Rote-Bete-Salat — so the head-noun entry is the authority.) Honest caveat for the operator: in everyday use 'Rote Bete' is mostly handled as a mass/collective, so the plural is uncommon in speech — but the classification decides the category (countable-thing / hasPlural TRUE) and the picture is one countable root, so a plural is required, and 'Rote Beten' is the attested one. Leaving an unattested zero would be worse.

bowling.why: Duden states it outright: 'das Bowling; Genitiv: des Bowlings, Plural: die Bowlings'. The stored zero plural 'Bowling' is not a form Duden gives. Both of Duden's Bedeutungen are the SPORT sense (amerikanische Art des Kegelspiels mit 10 Kegeln / englisches Kugelspiel auf glattem Rasen), so the attested plural sits on exactly the sense the key names — this is NOT the 'lettuce' case, where Duden's plural belonged to a sense the picture did not ask for. I re-fetched the entry to confirm before recording. CAVEAT for the operator: 'die Bowlings' is rare and unnatural in child speech; if you would rather this key never be pluralised, that is a content decision, not a form one — but the form Duden attests is Bowlings. Contrast the sibling 'camping', where Duden prints NO plural at all: this asymmetry is Duden's own, checked per word, not a rule I applied.

capybara.why: WEAKEST-EVIDENCE ROW IN THIS BATCH — flagged deliberately. Duden has NO Capybara entry (404) and DWDS answers 'nicht in unseren gegenwartssprachlichen lexikalischen Quellen vorhanden'. The only lexical authority I could reach is de.wiktionary, and it is explicit and positive rather than merely silent: its full declension table gives Nominativ Plural 'die Capybara' (Genitiv 'der Capybara', Dativ 'den Capybara'), and the Worttrennung line prints 'Plural: Ca·py·ba·ra'. No -s variant appears anywhere in the entry. So the stored 'Capybaras' is attested by no source I could fetch, while the zero plural is. I am NOT confident this is the whole truth: 'Capybaras' follows the productive -s pattern for vowel-final loans (Burritos, Kameras, Autos) and is common in real usage, so this may be a wiktionary gap rather than a genuine defect. If the operator can attest 'Capybaras', keep it and reject this fix. I record the fix because the evidence I actually have points one way, and I record the doubt because inventing confidence here would be the failure the brief punishes.

cauliflower.why: Duden prints the plural in full and it is not what is stored: 'der Blumenkohl; Genitiv: des Blumenkohls, Blumenkohles, Plural: die Blumenkohle'. The row holds the zero plural 'Blumenkohl', which Duden does not give. I re-fetched the raw Duden page a second time to be certain before recording it. Note the contrast with its own head noun: der Kohl is 'ohne Plural' (see the cabbage row), yet the compound Blumenkohl DOES have an attested plural — the two cannot be reasoned from one another, and raw countable:false is wrong here exactly as the brief warns for Spargel/Käse/Brokkoli.

coral.why: The stored plural merely repeats the singular ("Koralle"), which is simply wrong: Duden gives "die Koralle; Genitiv: der Koralle, Plural: die Korallen". The row's classification is countable-thing / hasPlural:true, and judged against the KEY (`coral` = the organism, as the ocean life art shows) die Koralle is an ordinary countable feminine noun. This is a pure form correction of the same word, so FIX rather than HOLD

dimetrodon.why: `Dimetrodone` is a builder invention (naive -e default). Duden: das Dimetrodon; Genitiv: des Dimetrodons, Plural: die Dimetrodonten — the Greek -odon stem takes -odonten.

diplodocus.why: Duden: der Diplodokus; Genitiv: des Diplodokus, Plural: die Diplodoken. Stored `Diplodocen` is not a Duden form.

durian.why: `Duriane` is a builder invention (naive -e default). Duden: die Durian; Genitiv: der Durian, Plural: die Durians. A loan — fetched, not reasoned from a class rule, per the brief's loan warning.

iguanodon.why: 'Iguanodone' is an INVENTED word — the builder's default -e append. Duden: 'das Iguanodon; Genitiv: des Iguanodons, Plural: die Iguanodons oder Iguanodonten'. Took Iguanodons (first-listed variant, and the child-friendlier one). NB the -saurus→-saurier rule correctly does NOT apply here: Iguanodon is Greek odon 'tooth', so it patterns with Mastodon→Mastodonten, not with Ichthyosaurus.

leek.why: Duden: 'der Lauch; Genitiv: des Lauches, Lauchs, Plural: die Lauche' — with NO 'ohne Plural' marker anywhere on the entry, and the row is classified hasPlural true. The stored zero plural 'Lauch' is not what Duden gives. This is NOT the lettuce case: Salat DOES carry an explicit 'ohne Plural' sense (which is why the last de round rightly rejected that fix) — Lauch carries none. Lauch also patterns with Spargel/Brokkoli, which the brief itself lists as wrongly marked uncountable. CAVEAT surfaced honestly: Duden's Bedeutung is 'in vielen Arten vorkommende Pflanze', so 'die Lauche' reads botanical/varietal; a child counting the depicted vegetable would more likely say 'zwei Lauchstangen'. Duden wins per the brief, but flagging the register for the operator.

lotus.why: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the stored plural "Lotusblüten" is the plural of a DIFFERENT lemma (die Lotusblüte), not of the stored singular "Lotus". Duden: "der Lotus; Genitiv: des Lotus, Plural: die Lotus" — a zero plural. Pure form fix on the same word.

medicine.why: DUDEN HAS THE PLURAL AND THE PICTURE IS THE SENSE THAT TAKES IT: "die Medizin; Genitiv: der Medizin, Plural: die Medizinen". The entry's "ohne Plural" flag belongs to the OTHER sense (Medizin = Heilkunde, the science). The depicted sense is Arznei — a bottle of medicine with tablets — exactly the countable one, and classification also says hasPlural: true. The stored field currently mirrors the singular, i.e. asserts no plural, which is wrong here. This is the INVERSE of the `lettuce` case the brief warns about: there the depicted sense LACKED Duden's plural; here it HAS it.

pepper.why: 🔴 THE PLURAL FIELD HOLDS A DIFFERENT WORD ENTIRELY. Stored plural is 'Pfeffer' — Duden: 'scharfes Gewürz ... in Form von [un]gemahlenen Pfefferkörnern', i.e. BLACK PEPPER, the spice. A child is shown a red bell pepper and taught 'Paprika → Pfeffer'. This is an EN-homonym collapse (English 'pepper' = both Paprika and Pfeffer) that a machine flattened. 🔴 I am OVERTURNING the prior de-08 verdict file, which ruled HOLD on all three fields on the grounds that it could not tell which image the key serves ('the second theme could host either image'). OPENING THE PICTURE ANSWERS THAT IN ONE SECOND — it is a bell pepper. That HOLD is precisely the failure this brief exists to end. Duden Paprika_Gemuese gives 'die Paprika; Plural: die Paprika, Paprikas und der Paprika; Plural: die Paprikas, Paprika' — I choose Paprikas because it is attested under BOTH gender readings, is unambiguously plural (unlike the zero-plural variant 'Paprika'), and matches the stored m gender.

pickup-truck.why: Duden: 'Plural: die Pick-ups'. The -s pattern in the stored value was already right; only the hyphen is missing.

potato-chips.why: plural-picture → hasPlural=false; once the singular field carries the plural label, the plural field has nothing further to derive. The stored 'Kartoffelchips' is the correct form and would simply mirror the corrected singular.

science.why: the builder left '-schaft' unchanged (its documented gap). Duden attests die Wissenschaft → die Wissenschaften ('die Akademie der Wissenschaften'); the current zero-form 'Wissenschaft' is not a plural

dimetrodon.why: Duden: Substantiv, NEUTRUM — das Dimetrodon, not *der. The `m` looks like a generic dinosaurs-are-masculine assumption; Duden contradicts it.

durian.why: Duden: Substantiv, FEMININ — die Durian, not *der Durian.

iguanodon.why: Duden: 'Substantiv, Neutrum' — das Iguanodon. Current m is wrong; likely copied from the -saurus siblings, which ARE maskulin.
